summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma on chemotherapy, was admitted with high fever, cough, and fatigue. He developed delirium, which resolved with treatment. Blood cultures identified E. coli bacteremia, and stool testing confirmed C. difficile infection. He was treated with IV meropenem, later transitioned to ertapenem via PICC, and oral vancomycin for C. diff. Imaging showed stable biliary stents, no source of infection was definitively identified, and brain imaging ruled out metastasis or acute intracranial pathology. His condition improved, mental status normalized, and he was discharged to extended care to complete antibiotic therapy with follow-up planned.
